candidates.title: Mobile Pointer 360 Browser Proof
candidates.why: Session 84 proved desktop pointer coverage, but the public launch promise is mobile and desktop. Running the same real-browser pointer sweep under a mobile viewport closes the biggest remaining automation gap before physical-device QA, and it catches canvas scaling regressions that unit tests cannot see.
candidates.recipe: Add a Mobile Chrome project to Playwright and make the pointer 360 spec assert viewport-specific coverage without changing the game loop. Keep the test path identical so desktop/mobile parity stays visible in one command.
executionLog: Playwright now runs the pointer 360 spec in Chromium and Mobile Chrome; npm run test:e2e passes 2/2.

candidates.title: First-Run Aim Check Chip
candidates.why: The game already remembers four-direction aim calibration, but first-run players only get prose guidance. A compact AIM CHECK chip turns that invisible trust state into a visible pre-run ritual, nudging players to prove full-circle aim before a serious run without adding a modal or account dependency.
candidates.recipe: Add buildInputCalibrationNudge(record, { debugEnabled }) in inputCalibration.js and render a quick chip on HomeV2 when totalRuns < 3 or debug input is enabled. Include focused tests for unverified, partial, complete, and debug states.
executionLog: HomeV2 renders an AIM CHECK chip for first-run/debug sessions, backed by tested calibration nudge states.

candidates.title: Death Heatmap Killer Label
candidates.why: The death heatmap now marks the final killer emoji, but the player still has to infer what it means. Rendering a small killer label and danger halo on the final marker makes the debrief instantly readable and completes the bounded first step before any heavier multi-death clustering work.
candidates.recipe: Extract buildGhostKillerMarker(ghostData, enemies, canvasSize) into a small utility, test its bounds and labels, and use it in DeathScreen to render emoji, name, and a final danger halo.
executionLog: DeathScreen now uses a tested ghost marker helper to draw final-killer emoji, name label, and danger halo on the ghost path.
